kinematics.note: Only the relative velocity fuses; a common drift is kinetic energy carried by both beams that the collision cannot use (it must be recovered). Co-propagating beams pay the drift twice: in the accelerator and in the recovery.

non_neutral.note: Pure-ion beams are limited by their own space charge (Brillouin density). Neutralising them admits electrons, which bring bremsstrahlung and electron drag: the burn becomes a beam-plasma system (section 4).

recirculation.note: Even with no electrons in the burn, every fusion costs ~ratio Coulomb events that each degrade beam energy and emittance. The heat left in hardware is (1 - eta) x restored power. The thermodynamic floor (k T ln growth per event at 1800 K) is ~1e-6 of the fusion energy: the bound is engineering, not the second law, but it needs near-reversible beam cooling.

control.note: Beyond a Debye length a single ion is screened: sensors and fields act on collective modes of ~N_D ions, never on one ion. Rutherford outcomes are random (impact parameter below the inter-particle spacing, femtometre-scale b0), so control can only correct after the fact, at the rate the scattering happens.

scale.note: Specific powers are declared HYPOTHESES (kW of processed power per kg of converter, supply, RF and cooling).
